answer: Each voting key must provision one exclusive last-mile peering inlet into a public exchange and lock a slashable bond. The circuit id is written to a public basalt registry so a reused port is obvious. At unscheduled times the exchange injects an ember probe, a short encrypted packet that only that live circuit may echo before the window closes. If two keys share an inlet, a probe is missed, or the echo comes from another port, every linked deposit is slashed. Fielding N identities needs N distinct circuits and N immobilized bonds, so access plant and capital scale with farm size.
